assumptions: The codon-usage table named, and Ikemura's definition of an optimal codon at the threshold given.
limits: Needs an in-frame CDS; scores codon choice only, not expression.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: Fop, RCBS and DCBS for the region, which the Codon optimality section shows as readouts under the cutoff that produced them; the gene's codon reading is on codon_usage_analysis.
bio.jane/contract.question: What share of this CDS's codons are the optimal ones for this host (Fop)?

description: Frequency of optimal codons (Fop, Ikemura 1981) for an in-frame CDS against a real codon-usage table: what share of its codons are the ones a highly-expressed gene in that host would use. Where CAI scores how CLOSE each codon is to its family's best, Fop scores only whether it IS one of the best, which makes it comparable across genes of different amino-acid composition. Name a table this project holds in `table`, or one of the bundled hosts in `host`.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

host.description: one of the three codon-usage tables bundled with the app. Only applies when table is not given.

sequence.description: the coding sequence, in frame (a length that is not a multiple of 3 is refused with the reason). Leave it empty to score the open record.

table.description: a codon-usage table this project holds, BY NAME, as the Codon Usage panel lists it — any organism. Takes precedence over `host`. This is the way to pass a table you fetched or built; `host` is only the three tables bundled with the app.

threshold.description: Ikemura's optimality cutoff: a codon counts as optimal at this share of its family's most-used codon. 0.8 is the convention, not a measurement, and the right value is host-dependent.

name: codon_optimality

nonOptimal.description: how many codons are NOT optimal (the honest denominator beside fop)

optimalCodons.description: size of the optimal set the reference defines

report.description: the full readout, including which host table answered

scored.description: codons that carried a call — stops and unevidenced families are excluded from both halves
